title: Development of an In Vitro 3D Model for Investigating Ligamentum Flavum Hypertrophy
author: Lin, Kuo, et al.
materials: The LF spheroids were first dissociated following the method reported by Grasser et al. [26] Several spheroids were collected from a ULA 96-well plate in a centrifuge tube (15 mL). After precipitation of the spheroids, the supernatants were carefully removed and washed twice with 1× PBS. Then, 1 mL of Accutase (Merck, Germany) was added, and the spheroids were resuspended 10 times using a 1000 μL pipette with a low-retention tip. The solution was transferred to a 12-well plate, incubated at 37 °C and shaken for 10 min, and the mixture was pipetted again. A visual microscopic inspection was performed to ensure that the spheroids were dissociated into single cells. If not, the incubation and pipetting steps were repeated until the spheroids dissociated into single cells. Finally, the mixture was centrifuged and washed with 1× PBS to remove the Accutase. The centrifuged pellet was fixed in ice-cold, 70% ethanol for 24 h at − 20 °C. The cells were washed twice with PBS and resuspended in 0.5 ml of propidium iodide (PI; BD Biosciences, USA) solution (20 μg/mL) containing RNase A (0.2 mg/mL) and 0.1% Triton X-100 (Sigma-Aldrich, USA) in 1× PBS for at least 15 min in the dark. Flow cytometric analyses were performed using a FACSCalibur system (BD Biosciences).

The cells were lysed in lysis buffer containing 1% Triton X-100, 50 mM Tris (pH 7.5), 10 mM EDTA, 0.02% NaN3 and a protease inhibitor mixture (Roche Diagnostics, Germany). The total protein concentration was measured by the Bradford method, and bovine serum albumin was used as a standard. Equal amounts of protein were separated by sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) on 10% or 7.5% gels. The resolved proteins were transferred onto polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membranes (Millipore, USA), which were then blocked with 5% nonfat dried milk in 1× PBS with 0.1% Tween® 20 detergent (PBST) for 1 h at room temperature before incubation overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies. Then, the PVDF membrane was washed with 1× PBST before incubation for 1 h at room temperature with the secondary antibody. The gels were then scanned using a laser scanner. The proteins were quantified using densitometry with the ImageJ.

steps.title: Collect and prepare LF tissue samples
steps.instruction: Obtain ligamentum flavum (LF) tissue from 12 patients (average age 60 years) undergoing posterior lumbar decompression and from control patients undergoing lumbar discectomy; exclude malignancy, vertebral fracture, infection, epidural or selective nerve‑root blocks. Remove epidural fat, wash tissues with 1× PBS, cut into small pieces, and place them in 10‑cm tissue‑culture‑treated dishes (Corning). Culture in DMEM (Gibco) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco) and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a humidified incubator, and replace medium 2–3 times per week.

steps.title: Expand primary LF cells and subculture
steps.instruction: Grow primary LF cells until 80–90 % confluency, then wash with 1× PBS and treat with 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA at 37 °C for 3 min. Add culture medium to inhibit trypsin, detach cells, and split at a 1:5 ratio, using only passages < 4. For immunofluorescence and histology assays, seed a total of 2 × 10⁵ cells (≈8 000 cells per 18 mm × 18 mm coverglass) in a 10‑cm petri dish containing the coverglass and culture for 24 h.

steps.title: Dissociate LF spheroids for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Collect several spheroids from a ULA 96‑well plate into a 15 mL centrifuge tube, wash twice with 1× PBS, add 1 mL Accutase (Merck) and resuspend by pipetting up and down 10 times with a 1000 µL low‑retention tip. Transfer to a 12‑well plate, incubate at 37 °C while shaking for 10 min, then pipette again. Microscopically verify single‑cell suspension; repeat incubation/pipetting if needed. Centrifuge, wash with PBS to remove Accutase, and fix the pellet in ice‑cold 70 % ethanol for 24 h at –20 °C. Wash twice with PBS and resuspend in 0.5 mL propidium iodide solution (20 µg/mL PI, 0.2 mg/mL RNase A, 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in 1× PBS) for at least 15 min in the dark.

steps.title: Perform flow cytometric analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the PI‑stained single‑cell suspension on a FACSCalibur flow cytometer (BD Biosciences) according to standard settings.

steps.title: Prepare protein lysates for western blot
steps.instruction: Lyse cells in buffer containing 1 % Triton X‑100, 50 mM Tris (pH 7.5), 10 mM EDTA, 0.02 % NaN₃ and a Roche protease‑inhibitor cocktail. Determine protein concentration by the Bradford assay using bovine serum albumin as standard. Mix equal amounts of protein with loading buffer and load onto SDS‑PAGE gels (10 % or 7.5 % acrylamide).

steps.title: Transfer and immunoblot proteins
steps.instruction: Transfer separated proteins onto PVDF membranes (Millipore). Block membranes with 5 % non‑fat dried milk in 1× PBS containing 0.1 % Tween 20 (PBST) for 1 h at room temperature. Incubate membranes overnight at 4 °C with the appropriate primary antibodies. Wash membranes with 1× PBST, then incubate with secondary antibody for 1 h at room temperature. Scan the membranes with a laser scanner and quantify band intensities using ImageJ densitometry.

steps.title: Analyze data statistically
steps.instruction: Present data as mean ± standard deviation, compare groups using one‑way ANOVA, consider p < 0.05 statistically significant, and perform all analyses with Prism 8 (GraphPad Software).
